title: Exact identifiability does not guarantee stable recovery
problem: Choose additional directional line-sum measurements for a square lattice after four fixed projections.
failure: A minimum-cost full-rank design meets exact uniqueness but is not necessarily a stable inverse. On the 10x10 grid the extra normal (1,7) has 73 occupied bins yet minimum singular value about 0.079; (1,8) costs 82 and has about 0.291. This is a counterexample to treating uniqueness as sufficient for choosing a stable design, not a failure of the uniqueness theorem.
correction: State the readout-cost and noise model separately; establish injectivity, then measure the actual observation matrix's smallest singular value. Compare cost versus amplification and retain numerical and physical limitations.
transfer: In any linear inverse problem, distinguish structural rank from quantitative conditioning. Do not deploy a minimum-cost identifiable design solely on the basis of rank; assess sensitivity using a noise model appropriate to the actual instruments.
limits: R07 exact bin-count theorem assumes primitive integer normals and per-occupied-bin cost. Bounded NumPy SVD comparison assumes additive Euclidean error and unconstrained least squares. No actual noise simulation, physical tests, independent review or claim of global conditioning optimum.
